# TechLead Decomposition Build Arrow Diagram

## Purpose

Show the intended extraction path from the current `techlead.py` hub into bounded service components without restarting the whole design.

## Current Source

- `/Users/billyweisberg/Repos/billyweisberg/paa-platform/packages/paa-consumer/src/paa_consumer/techlead.py`

## Build Arrow Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  MONO["paa_consumer.techlead.py\ncurrent hybrid hub"] --> ASSIGN["TechLeadAssignmentDecisionService\nassignment decision extraction"]
  MONO --> REVIEW["TechLeadWorkerReviewRoutingService\nworker-result and QA-routing extraction"]
  MONO --> ACCEPT["TechLeadAcceptanceDecisionService\nacceptance and closeout extraction"]

  ASSIGN --> CORE_ASSIGN["packages/paa-core/src/paa_core/services/techlead_assignment_decision/"]
  REVIEW --> CORE_REVIEW["packages/paa-core/src/paa_core/services/techlead_worker_review_routing/"]
  ACCEPT --> CORE_ACCEPT["packages/paa-core/src/paa_core/services/techlead_acceptance_decision/"]

  MONO --> SHELL["remaining paa_consumer runtime shell\nCLI / transport / composition only"]

  CORE_ASSIGN --> SHELL
  CORE_REVIEW --> SHELL
  CORE_ACCEPT --> SHELL
```

## Intended End State

`paa-consumer` should retain:
- runtime shell composition
- packet claim/send integration
- queue and worktree operations
- CLI adapters

`paa-core` should own:
- assignment decision logic
- worker review routing logic
- acceptance decision logic
- typed request / result models for those services

## Non-Goals

This diagram does not introduce new packet families or a new top-level runtime architecture.
It only defines the extraction path inside the existing scaffold.
